Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bag 0.5.0

The package is renamed from spacehakr to bag, every exported function is renamed with it, and ten functions are gone. Nothing written against spacehakr 0.4.2 keeps working. Install NewGraphEnvironment/spacehakr@v0.4.2 for the old package — the tag still resolves through GitHub’s repository redirect.

The subject is now one thing: fetching public data and field files to disk.

The name

spacehakr described a grab-bag of spatial helpers. The package no longer is one, so the name no longer described it. bag is what it does — it fetches things and puts them somewhere.

The old pkgdown site at www.newgraphenvironment.com/spacehakr/ goes dark. GitHub redirects repository URLs but not Pages paths. The site is now www.newgraphenvironment.com/bag/.

Functions that stayed, renamed

spacehakr 0.4.2 bag 0.5.0
spk_source_url() bag_url()
spk_source_bcdata() bag_bcdc()
spk_geoserv_dlv() bag_wfs()
spk_layer_info() bag_layers()

Functions removed

spk_gdalwarp(), spk_join(), spk_odm(), spk_poly_to_points(), spk_q_layer_info(), spk_rast_ext(), spk_rast_not_empty(), spk_rast_rm_empty(), spk_res() and spk_stac_calc(). These were raster, drone-imagery and STAC helpers — a different subject — and nothing called them under these names.

ngr keeps serving all ten, and it is pinned so that it can. Its ngr_spk_* functions are deprecating forwarders whose bodies call spacehakr::spk_*(), and it carries spacehakr in Imports:. So ngr pins NewGraphEnvironment/spacehakr@v0.4.2, the last release before this one, and keeps installing a package that still has them. Code calling ngr_spk_* is unaffected.

Retiring those forwarders — re-pointing the two whose targets survive here under new names, rehoming the four that have callers and no successor, deleting the six that have neither — is tracked in ngr rather than here.

The two pkgdown articles went with them: both documented only spk_stac_calc().

Functions added

Ten. Eleven were taken in from two older first-party packages whose subject is reporting rather than fetching; one of those, a GeoPackage layer remover, was then dropped again (below).

Nothing calling the old names breaks, because those packages still hold their own copies of these functions — they are not forwarders yet. Adding deprecating forwarders, so the two do not drift apart, is tracked in each of them.

  • BC Data Catalogue: bag_bcdc_read() reads a record into memory, bag_bcdc_index() builds a lookup of every catalogue layer with a WMS resource, bag_bcdc_cols() describes one column.
  • Files: bag_gpx_import() reads a GPS unit’s GPX files into a GeoPackage, bag_gpkg_to_geojson() writes each layer of a GeoPackage out as GeoJSON, bag_backup() copies a file into a backup directory with a timestamp, and bag_gpkg_refresh() refreshes a point GeoPackage’s coordinate columns.
  • Coordinates: bag_assign_utm() and bag_assign_latlong() write coordinate columns onto an sf object; bag_sf_from_utm() builds an sf object from UTM columns.

Nine defects were found and fixed while porting these, and each was reported to the package it came from. Among them: a geometry guard that could never fire, written as !x != y where ! binds looser than !=; a GPX timestamp filter that compared a UTC instant against a machine-local one; and a GeoPackage layer remover with a data-loss path, which was then dropped from this package altogether as superseded upstream.

Other changes

  • magrittr is not a dependency. The donated functions arrived with magrittr pipelines and were rewritten to the native pipe.
  • Dependencies. Imports is 15, from 14: terra and xml2 went with the deleted helpers, and janitor, lubridate and readr arrived with the intake. Suggests is 5, from 12: grDevices, kableExtra, knitr, leafem, leaflet, mapview, processx, rmarkdown, rstac and stars were all there for the deleted functions and their articles, and DBI and RSQLite arrived for the GeoPackage fixtures the new tests build.
  • The pkgdown reference index is grouped by @family, so it now fails the build when an export is missing from it. It previously had no reference: section at all, which made pkgdown::check_pkgdown() vacuous.
  • The package has a .lintr config for the first time. lintr::lint_package() is clean.
  • R CMD check is 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
